You likely don't want these settings to be applied in every file, so make sure that you add a &#96;overrides&#96; section in your &#96;.eslintrc.*&#96; file that applies the overrides only to your stories files.\n\n.eslintrc\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"overrides\": [\n    {\n      // 👇 This should match the &#96;stories&#96; property in .storybook/main.js|ts\n      \"files\": ['**/*.stories.@(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)'],\n      \"rules\": {\n        // 👇 Enable this rule\n        'storybook/csf-component': 'error',\n        // 👇 Disable this rule\n        'storybook/default-exports': 'off',\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Configuration (flat config format)\n\nUse &#96;eslint.config.js&#96; file to configure rules using the flat config style. This is the default in ESLint v9, but can be used starting from ESLint v8.57.0\\. See also: \u003chttps://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/configuration-files-new\u003e.\n\neslint.config.js\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport storybook from 'eslint-plugin-storybook';\n \nexport default [\n  // Add more generic rulesets here, such as:\n  // js.configs.recommended,\n  ...storybook.configs['flat/recommended'],\n \n  // ...\n];\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn case you are using utility functions from tools like &#96;tseslint&#96;, you might need to register the plugin a little differently:\n\neslint.config.ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport storybook from 'eslint-plugin-storybook';\nimport somePlugin from 'some-plugin';\nimport tseslint from 'typescript-eslint';\n \nexport default tseslint.config(\n  somePlugin,\n  storybook.configs['flat/recommended'] // notice that it is not destructured\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Overriding/disabling rules\n\nOptionally, you can override, add, or disable individual rules. file\n!.storybook\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis allows for this plugin to also lint your configuration files inside the .storybook folder, so that you always have a correct configuration and don't face You can omit the &#96;eslint-plugin-&#96; prefix:\n\n{\n  \"plugins\": [\"storybook\"]\n}\n\nThen, define which rule configurations to extend in your eslint file. Before that, it's important to understand that **Storybook linting rules should only be applied in your stories files**. You don't want rules to affect your other files such as production or test code as the rules might conflict with rules from other ESLint plugins.\n\n### Run the plugin only against story files\n\nWe don't want &#96;eslint-plugin-storybook&#96; to run against your whole codebase. To run this plugin only against your stories files, you have the following options:\n\n#### ESLint &#96;overrides&#96; \n\nOne way of restricting ESLint config by file patterns is by using ESLint overrides.\n\nAssuming you are using the recommended &#96;.stories&#96; extension in your files, the following config would run &#96;eslint-plugin-storybook&#96; only against your stories files:\n\n// .eslintrc\n{\n  // 1) Here we have our usual config which applies to the whole project, so we don't put storybook preset here.\n  \"extends\": [\"airbnb\", \"plugin:prettier/recommended\"],\n\n  // 2) We load eslint-plugin-storybook globally with other ESLint plugins.\n  \"plugins\": [\"react-hooks\", \"storybook\"],\n\n  \"overrides\": [\n    {\n      // 3) Now we enable eslint-plugin-storybook rules or preset only for matching files!\n      // you can use the one defined in your main.js\n      \"files\": ['src/**/*.stories.@(js|jsx|ts|tsx)'],\n      \"extends\": [\"plugin:storybook/recommended\"],\n\n      // 4) Optional: you can override specific rules here if you want. Else delete this\n      \"rules\": {\n        'storybook/no-redundant-story-name': 'error'\n      }\n    },\n  ],\n};\n\n#### ESLint Cascading and Hierarchy\n\nAnother approach for customizing ESLint config by paths is through ESLint Cascading and Hierarchy. This is useful if all your stories are placed under the same folder, so you can place there another &#96;.eslintrc&#96; where you enable &#96;eslint-plugin-storybook&#96; for applying it only to the It is responsible for the following:\n\n* the main UI of storybook\n* the UI used by addons\n* the API used by addons\n* the API used by the CLI\n* the API used by the server\n* prebundled code used by the browser\n* static assets used by the browser\n* utilities for CSF, MDX \u0026 Docs\n\n## Private package\n\nThis package is not intended to be used by anyone but storybook internally.\n\nEven though this is where all of the code is located, it is NOT to be the entry point when using functionality within!\n\nConsumers of the code should import like so:\n\nimport { addons } from 'storybook/manager-api';\n\nImporting from &#96;@storybook/core&#96; (and ONLY from &#96;@storybook/core&#96;):\n\n* &#96;@storybook/core&#96;\n* &#96;@storybook/codemod&#96;\n\nTo prevent cyclical dependencies, these packages cannot depend on the &#96;storybook&#96; package.\n\n## When to use &#96;storybook/internal&#96; \n\nIn every other package you should import from &#96;storybook/internal&#96; (and ONLY from &#96;storybook/internal&#96;).\n\nThe heuristic is simple:\n\n\u003e If you see a peerDependency on &#96;storybook&#96; * Documentation  \n   * Frameworks  \n   * Reproduce  \n   * Roadmap\n* FAQ\n* Migrate to 9.0  \n   * Migrate from 7.x to 8.0\n\n# ESLint plugin\n\nStorybook provides an dedicated ESLint plugin to help you write stories and components aligned with the latest Storybook and frontend development best practices.\n\n## Installation\n\nYou'll first need to install ESLint:\n\nnpm\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpm install --save-dev eslint\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNext, install &#96;eslint-plugin-storybook&#96;:\n\nnpm\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpm install --save-dev eslint-plugin-storybook\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThen add &#96;plugin:storybook/recommended&#96; to the extends section of your &#96;.eslintrc&#96; configuration file. Note that we can omit the &#96;eslint-plugin-&#96; prefix:\n\n.eslintrc\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  // extend plugin:storybook/\u003cconfiguration\u003e, such as:\n  \"extends\": [\"plugin:storybook/recommended\"]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAnd finally, add this to your &#96;.eslintignore&#96; file:\n\n.eslintignore\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n!.storybook\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis ensures that the plugin will also lint your configuration files inside the &#96;.storybook&#96; directory, so that you always have a correct configuration. For example, it can catch mistyped addon names in your &#96;main.js|ts&#96; file.\n\nFor more details on why this line is required in the &#96;.eslintignore&#96; file, refer to the ESLint documentation.\n\nIf you are using flat config style, add this to your configuration file:\n\neslint.config.js\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nexport default [\n  // ...\n  {\n    // Inside your .eslintignore file\n    ignores: ['!.storybook'],\n  },\n];\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## ESLint compatibility\n\nDepending on the version of ESLint you are using, you may need to install a specific version of the Storybook plugin. Use the table below to match the plugin version to your ESLint version.\n\n| ESLint version | Storybook plugin version |\n| -------------- | ------------------------ |\n| ^9.0.0         | ^9.0.0 or ^0.10.0        |\n| ^8.57.0        | ^9.0.0 or ^0.10.0        |\n| ^7.0.0         | \\~0.9.0                  |\n\n## Usage\n\n### Configuration (.eslintrc)\n\nUse &#96;.eslintrc.*&#96; file to configure rules in ESLint \u003c v9\\. See also: \u003chttps://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/\u003e.\n\nThis plugin will only be applied to files following the &#96;*.stories.*&#96; (we recommend this) or &#96;*.story.*&#96; pattern. This is an automatic configuration, so you don't have to do anything.\n\n#### Overriding/disabling rules\n\nOptionally, you can override, add, or disable individual rules. You likely don't want these settings to be applied in every file, so make sure that you add a &#96;overrides&#96; section in your &#96;.eslintrc.*&#96; file that applies the overrides only to your stories files.\n\n.eslintrc\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"overrides\": [\n    {\n      // 👇 This should match the &#96;stories&#96; property in .storybook/main.js|ts\n      \"files\": ['**/*.stories.@(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)'],\n      \"rules\": {\n        // 👇 Enable this rule\n        'storybook/csf-component': 'error',\n        // 👇 Disable this rule\n        'storybook/default-exports': 'off',\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Configuration (flat config format)\n\nUse &#96;eslint.config.js&#96; file to configure rules using the flat config style. This is the default in ESLint v9, but can be used starting from ESLint v8.57.0\\. See also: \u003chttps://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/configuration-files-new\u003e.\n\neslint.config.js\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport storybook from 'eslint-plugin-storybook';\n \nexport default [\n  // Add more generic rulesets here, such as:\n  // js.configs.recommended,\n  ...storybook.configs['flat/recommended'],\n \n  // ...\n];\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn case you are using utility functions from tools like &#96;tseslint&#96;, you might need to register the plugin a little differently:\n\neslint.config.ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport storybook from 'eslint-plugin-storybook';\nimport somePlugin from 'some-plugin';\nimport tseslint from 'typescript-eslint';\n \nexport default tseslint.config(\n  somePlugin,\n  storybook.configs['flat/recommended'] // notice that it is not destructured\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Overriding/disabling rules\n\nOptionally, you can override, add, or disable individual rules. You likely don't want these settings to be applied in every file, so make sure that you add a flat config section in your &#96;eslint.config.js&#96; file that applies the overrides only to your stories files.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport storybook from 'eslint-plugin-storybook';\n \nexport default [\n  // ...\n \n  ...storybook.configs['flat/recommended'],\n  {\n    // 👇 This should match the &#96;stories&#96; property in .storybook/main.js|ts\n    files: ['**/*.stories.@(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)'],\n    rules: {\n      // 👇 Enable this rule\n      'storybook/csf-component': 'error',\n      // 👇 Disable this rule\n      'storybook/default-exports': 'off',\n    },\n  },\n \n  // ...\n];\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### MDX Support\n\nThis plugin does not support MDX files.\n\n## Supported Rules and configurations\n\n**Configurations**: csf, csf-strict, addon-interactions, recommended\n\n| Name You likely don't want these settings to be applied in every file, so make sure that you add a &#96;overrides&#96; section in your &#96;.eslintrc.*&#96; file that applies the overrides only to your stories files.\n\n{\n  \"overrides\": [\n    {\n      // or whatever matches stories specified in .storybook/main.js\n      \"files\": ['**/*.stories.@(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)'],\n      \"rules\": {\n        // example of overriding a rule\n        'storybook/hierarchy-separator': 'error',\n        // example of disabling a rule\n        'storybook/default-exports': 'off',\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n\n### Configuration (&#96;eslint.config.[c|m]?js&#96;)\n\nUse &#96;eslint.config.[c|m]?js&#96; file to configure rules using the flat config style. This is the default in ESLint v9, but can be used starting from ESLint v8.57.0\\. See also: \u003chttps://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/configuration-files-new\u003e.\n\nimport storybook from 'eslint-plugin-storybook'\n\nexport default [\n  // add more generic rulesets here, such as:\n  // js.configs.recommended,\n  ...storybook.configs['flat/recommended'],\n\n  // something ...\n]\n\nIn case you are using utility functions from tools like &#96;tseslint&#96;, you might need to set the plugin a little differently:\n\nimport storybook from \"eslint-plugin-storybook\";\n\nimport somePlugin from 'some-plugin';\nimport tseslint from 'typescript-eslint';\nexport default tseslint.config(\n  somePlugin,\n  storybook.configs[\"flat/recommended\"] // notice that it is not destructured\n);\"\n\n#### Overriding/disabling rules\n\nOptionally, you can override, add or disable rules settings. You likely don't want these settings to be applied in every file, so make sure that you add a flat config section in your &#96;eslint.config.[m|c]?js&#96; file that applies the overrides only to your stories files.\n\nimport storybook from 'eslint-plugin-storybook'\n\nexport default [\n  // ...\n\n  ...storybook.configs['flat/recommended'],\n  {\n    files: ['**/*.stories.@(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)'],\n    rules: {\n      // example of overriding a rule\n      'storybook/hierarchy-separator': 'error',\n      // example of disabling a rule\n      'storybook/default-exports': 'off',\n    },\n  },\n\n  // something ...\n]\n\n### MDX Support\n\nThis plugin does not support MDX files.\n\n## Supported Rules and configurations\n\n**Key**: 🔧 =       "chunk": "skip to:contentpackage searchsign in\n\n❤\n\n* Pro\n* Teams\n* Pricing\n* Documentation\n\nnpm\n\nSearch\n\nSign UpSign In\n\n## @chanzuckerberg/eslint-plugin-stories\n\nTypeScript icon, indicating that this package has built-in type declarations\n\n3.2.14 • Public • Published 2 years ago\n\n* Readme\n* Code Beta\n* 0 Dependencies\n* 0 Dependents\n* 36 Versions\n\n# eslint-plugin-stories\n\nESLint rules for Storybook stories.\n\nIn particular, these rules ensure that stories can be used in non-Storybook contexts. For example, for accessibility testing via axe-storybook-testing, or visual regression testing via percy-storybook.\n\n## Installation\n\nInstall @chanzuckerberg/eslint-plugin-stories with your favorite package manager. With yarn, that would look like\n\nyarn add --dev @chanzuckerberg/eslint-plugin-stories\n\n## Usage\n\nAdd @chanzuckerberg/stories as a plugin in your eslint configuration file.\n\n// .eslintrc.json\n{\n  \"plugins\": [\"@chanzuckerberg/stories\"]\n}\n\nThen you can either extend the recommended config to turn on all the rules\n\n// .eslintrc.json\n{\n  \"extends\": [\"plugin:@chanzuckerberg/stories/recommended\"]\n}\n\nor configure the rules individually\n\n// .eslintrc.json\n{\n  \"rules\": {\n    \"@chanzuckerberg/stories/no-ext-resources-in-stories\": \"warn\"\n  }\n}\n\n## Rules\n\n| Name                           | Description                                                                                                | Config      |\n| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |\n| csf-object-literal-or-function | Enforce that stories are either an object literal or function.                                             | recommended |\n| csf-v3-types                   | Enforce component story format (CSF) v3 stories have explicit TypeScript types where needed for inferrence | strict      |\n| no-csf-v2                      | Use object stories (component story format v3) instead of functions.                                       | strict      |\n| no-ext-resources-in-stories    | Prevent external resources from being loaded in stories.                                                   | recommended |\n| no-components-without-story    | Enforce that new components are created with a corresponding story                                         | strict      |\n\n## Readme\n\n### Keywords\n\n* eslint\n*       "chunk": "DocsAddonsShowcaseBlogVisual TestEnterprise\n\n87,172\n\nSearch docs\n\n⌃K\n\nBack to blog\n\nJoin the community:\n\n# How to use Storybook with ESLint\n\nAutomatically validate stories in your code editor\n\nloading\n\nYann Braga\n\nDec 22, 2021 — @yannbf\n\nLast updated: Dec 22, 2021\n\nStorybook is used by thousands of teams at companies like Audi, Twilio, and Spotify. Our community develops everything from atomic UI components all the way to pages in isolation with Storybook. Along the way, developers write countless stories.\n\nEven though stories follow CSF, a standard ES6-based format, it can still be tough to catch typos and syntax errors. Or to know which practices are officially recommended by the team. \n\nI’m excited to share Storybook’s official ESLint plugin, an automated tool that helps you write stories with greater consistency and fewer mistakes. You’ll spend less time fixing errors in stories because you won’t make them at all.\n\n* ✅ Validate story code as you write it\n* 🗂 Standardize how you write stories across projects\n* 📐 12 rules and counting\n\n  \n## Why create an ESLint plugin?\n\nStorybook’s core innovation is the “story” construct. Stories isolate and capture component examples in a standard, ES6-based format. \n\nBut sometimes stories don’t quite work because of typos, syntax errors, or folks forgetting the default export. Other times, you might want to try the latest Storybook features like addon-interactions but don’t have the right libraries to use it. These issues are straightforward to fix but easy to miss. \n\nWe’re building **eslint-plugin-storybook** to keep story code up to standards and ensure that everyone follows the best practices.\n\nWhat’s more, when your code adheres to a consistent format, you can take advantage of Storybook’s auto-migrations and codemods that get shipped with minor/major releases. That means keeping up to date requires even less work from you.\n\n## See it in action\n\nThere are currently 12 rules in the plugin that show errors and warnings along with helpful suggestions. The ruleset will keep evolving with new rules added over time. Here are a few use cases where the plugin helps:  \n  \n**Write stories from scratch**  \nThe storybook/story-exports and storybook/default-exportswill make sure that your file contains a default export (known as meta) and at least one named export. This is necessary for Storybook to identify your component stories.\n\n**Migrate from the legacy storiesOf api**  \nThe storybook/no-stories-of can help teammates avoid using the legacy story syntax that’s no longer in active development and will be deprecated in future versions of Storybook.\n\n**Write interactive stories with the new addon-interactions**  \nIn the GIF below, you can see the linter fixing three different rules related to the play function and addon-interactions: storybook/await-interactions, storybook/use-storybook-expect and storybook/use-storybook-testing-library.\n\n**Codemods for automatic migration**  \nStorybook provides codemods for automatic migration when there are API changes. In 6.4, this is baked into the &#96;npx sb upgrade&#96; command. But codemods only work when the code follows standards. Our linter plugin ensures that your code follows Storybook standards and thus will always be able to get auto-migrated.\n\n**And many more lint rules**  \nInstall the plugin to discover all the rules. If you have questions about a rule, follow the contextual link to a documentation where the rule is explained, along with correct and incorrect examples.  \n\n##   \nGet started with Storybook + ESLint\n\nIf you already use ESLint in your project, first try Storybook's automigration to add and configure the linter automatically for you:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpx sb@latest automigrate\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Manual install**  \nInstall the plugin manually if the auto-migration wasn’t compatible with your project setup. You'll first need to install ESLint if you don't have already:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpm install eslint --save-dev\n# or\nyarn add eslint --dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNext, install eslint-plugin-storybook:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpm install eslint-plugin-storybook --save-dev\n# or\nyarn add eslint-plugin-storybook --dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNow that the plugin is installed, all you have to do is add \"plugin:storybook/recommended\" to the extends section of your &#96;.eslintrc&#96; configuration file:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  // extend plugin:storybook/\u003cconfiguration\u003e, such as:\n  \"extends\": [\"plugin:storybook/recommended\"]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis linter will only run against files following the &#96;*.stories.*&#96; (we recommend this) or &#96;*.story.*&#96; pattern. This is an automatic configuration, so you don't have to do anything!\n\n**Configure the plugin**  \nFollow the instructions here to change how the plugin behaves. For example, ignore rules or throw errors instead of warnings.\n\n## Get involved\n\nThe eslint-plugin is developed by Yann Braga (me!) and Michael Shilman, with feedback from the entire Storybook community. Special thanks to Kyle Gach, Norbert de Langen, Tom Coleman, and Oscar Dominguez for the early feedback, as well as Rafael Rozon for originally creating the library.  \n  \nThe project is maintained by 1,400+ open source contributors and guided by a steering committee. If you are interested in contributing, check out Storybook on GitHub, create an issue, or submit a pull request.\n\nChat with us in Discord — a maintainer is usually online. Donate on Open Collective. Stay up to date with Storybook news on Twitter and by signing up for our mailing list below.\n\n\u003e Storybook's ESLint plugin is here!  \n\u003e  \n\u003e ✅ Validate story code as you write it   \n\u003e 🗂 Standardize how you write stories across projects  \n\u003e ✨ Simplifies auto-migration bw versions via codemods  \n\u003e  \n\u003e Install it:https://t.co/JbdD9lEi3L  \n\u003e  \n\u003e Shoutout to @yannbf @mshilman @geteslint\n\u003e \n\u003e — Storybook (@storybookjs) December 22, 2021\n\n### Join the Storybook mailing list\n\nGet the latest news, updates and releases\n\nYour email\n\nSend\n\n7,216 developers and counting\n\n### We’re hiring!\n\nJoin the team behind Storybook and Chromatic. Build tools that are used in production by 100s of thousands of developers. Remote-first.\n\nView jobs\n\nESLint\n\n## Popular posts\n\nState of Storybook 2021Huge year for performance, testing, and community ecosystem\n\nloading\n\nMichael Shilman\n\nDec 29, 2021\n\nDesign integrations for StorybookHow to integrate design tools with Storybook\n\nloading\n\nDominic Nguyen\n\nJan 05, 2022\n\nComponent Encyclopedia sneak peekBrowse the world’s UI components to discover techniques that work\n\nloading\n\nDominic Nguyen\n\nDec 08, 2021\n\nJoin the community\n\nYour email\n\nSubscribe\n\n7,216 developers and counting\n\nWhyWhy StorybookComponent-driven UI\n\nDocsGuidesTutorialsChangelogTelemetry\n\nCommunityAddonsGet involvedBlog\n\nShowcaseExploreProjectsComponent glossary\n\nOpen source software\n\nStorybook\n\n---\n\nMaintained by\n\nChromatic\n\nSpecial thanks to Netlify and CircleCI",
      "title": "How to use Storybook with ESLint",

      "chunk": "skip to:contentpackage searchsign in\n\n❤\n\n* Pro\n* Teams\n* Pricing\n* Documentation\n\nnpm\n\nSearch\n\nSign UpSign In\n\n## eslint-plugin-storybook\n\nTypeScript icon, indicating that this package has built-in type declarations\n\n0.0.1-alpha.0 • Public • Published 4 years ago\n\n* Readme\n* Code Beta\n* 1 Dependency\n* 383 Dependents\n* 374 Versions\n\nStorybook \n\nBuild bulletproof UI components faster\n\n  \nStorybook Community Backers on Open Collective Sponsors on Open Collective Official Twitter Handle \n\n# eslint-plugin-storybook\n\nBest practice rules for Storybook\n\n## Installation\n\nYou'll first need to install ESLint:\n\nnpm i eslint --save-dev\n\nNext, install &#96;eslint-plugin-storybook&#96;:\n\nnpm install eslint-plugin-storybook --save-dev\n\n## Usage\n\nAdd &#96;storybook&#96; to the plugins section of your &#96;.eslintrc&#96; configuration file. You can omit the &#96;eslint-plugin-&#96; prefix:\n\n{\n  \"plugins\": [\"storybook\"]\n}\n\nThen, define which rule configurations to extend in your eslint file. Before that, it's important to understand that **Storybook linting rules should only be applied in your stories files**. You don't want rules to affect your other files such as production or test code as the rules might conflict with rules from other ESLint plugins.\n\n### Run the plugin only against story files\n\nWe don't want &#96;eslint-plugin-storybook&#96; to run against your whole codebase. To run this plugin only against your stories files, you have the following options:\n\n#### ESLint &#96;overrides&#96; \n\nOne way of restricting ESLint config by file patterns is by using ESLint overrides.\n\nAssuming you are using the recommended &#96;.stories&#96; extension in your files, the following config would run &#96;eslint-plugin-storybook&#96; only against your stories files:\n\n// .eslintrc\n{\n  // 1) Here we have our usual config which applies to the whole project, so we don't put storybook preset here.\n  \"extends\": [\"airbnb\", \"plugin:prettier/recommended\"],\n\n  // 2) We load eslint-plugin-storybook globally with other ESLint plugins.\n  \"plugins\": [\"react-hooks\", \"storybook\"],\n\n  \"overrides\": [\n    {\n      // 3) Now we enable eslint-plugin-storybook rules or preset only for matching files!\n      // you can use the one defined in your main.js\n      \"files\": ['src/**/*.stories.@(js|jsx|ts|tsx)'],\n      \"extends\": [\"plugin:storybook/recommended\"],\n\n      // 4) Optional: you can override specific rules here if you want. Else delete this\n      \"rules\": {\n        'storybook/no-redundant-story-name': 'error'\n      }\n    },\n  ],\n};\n\n#### ESLint Cascading and Hierarchy\n\nAnother approach for customizing ESLint config by paths is through ESLint Cascading and Hierarchy. This is useful if all your stories are placed under the same folder, so you can place there another &#96;.eslintrc&#96; where you enable &#96;eslint-plugin-storybook&#96; for applying it only to the files under such folder, rather than enabling it on your global &#96;.eslintrc&#96; which would apply to your whole project.\n\n## Supported Rules\n\n**Key**: 🔧 \\= fixable\n\n**Configurations**: csf, csf-strict, addon-interactions, recommended\n\n| Name                                                                                                                                                    | Description                                       | 🔧               | Included in configurations      |\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------- |\n| [storybook/csf-component](https://github.com/storybookjs/eslint-plugin-storybook/blob/HEAD/docs/rules/csf-component.md)                                 | The component property should be set              | csf              |                                 |\n| [storybook/default-exports](https://github.com/storybookjs/eslint-plugin-storybook/blob/HEAD/docs/rules/default-exports.md)                             | Story files should have a default export          | csf, recommended |                                 |\n| [storybook/hierarchy-separator](https://github.com/storybookjs/eslint-plugin-storybook/blob/HEAD/docs/rules/hierarchy-separator.md)                     | Deprecated hierachy separator in title property   | 🔧               | csf, recommended                |\n| [storybook/meta-inline-properties](https://github.com/storybookjs/eslint-plugin-storybook/blob/HEAD/docs/rules/meta-inline-properties.md)               | Meta should only have inline properties           | csf, recommended |                                 |\n| [storybook/no-redundant-story-name](https://github.com/storybookjs/eslint-plugin-storybook/blob/HEAD/docs/rules/no-redundant-story-name.md)             | A story should not have a redundant name property | 🔧               | csf, recommended                |\n| [storybook/no-stories-of](https://github.com/storybookjs/eslint-plugin-storybook/blob/HEAD/docs/rules/no-stories-of.md)                                 | storiesOf is deprecated and should not be used    | csf-strict       |                                 |\n| [storybook/no-title-property-in-meta](https://github.com/storybookjs/eslint-plugin-storybook/blob/HEAD/docs/rules/no-title-property-in-meta.md)         | Do not define a title in meta                     | 🔧               | csf-strict                      |\n| [storybook/prefer-pascal-case](https://github.com/storybookjs/eslint-plugin-storybook/blob/HEAD/docs/rules/prefer-pascal-case.md)                       | Stories should use PascalCase                     | 🔧               | recommended                     |\n| [storybook/use-storybook-expect](https://github.com/storybookjs/eslint-plugin-storybook/blob/HEAD/docs/rules/use-storybook-expect.md)                   | Use expect from @storybook/jest                   | 🔧               | addon-interactions, recommended |\n| [storybook/use-storybook-testing-library](https://github.com/storybookjs/eslint-plugin-storybook/blob/HEAD/docs/rules/use-storybook-testing-library.md) | Do not use testing-library directly on stories
